intro: A collection of my thoughts, observations, and quick notes on writing, code, and life.

jots.title: Grateful for Rain 🌦️
jots.content:
They say it never rains in Southern California. Around 90% of the year, that's true. It wasn't long ago that we went through a rough stretch of 4 or 5 years without any significant rain, along with average temps of 95+ all year. It was brutal.

 The last few years has brought more moisture, however, it's not lost on me that for many areas closer to the coast, it can be too much all at once. So, while I'm grateful for the moderate rainfall here, closer to the deserts, I'm still thinking of those prone to flood.

 I won't go into detail, here and now, as to be mindful of the current situation. However, I plan on going further on the impact of human infrastructure as it pertains to flooding.

 For now, though, I'll just be grateful that the roses get another hardy drink (more forecasted on the way) and focus on the positive.

 * On a related note, [AI Architecture Lab is working on a SeeJoshsPhotos app experience](index.html?=page:seejoshsphotos), as we speak. I am also considering a flowers-only experience as a companion project.

 In due time...

jots.title: No Matter How
jots.content:
“Never fear another challenger, no matter how large; never despise another challenger, no matter how small. Large does not always defeat little. Little can become large by constant building; large can become little by falling apart.”

 -- Morihei Ueshiba

jots.title: Trust the Rest
jots.content:
Part of me is anxious to rush this process. I'm exited anout building my own space from scratch, and can't wait to connect the domain and start sharing it but, I am trying to embrace patience. 

 I've been working with AI for a few weeks now, and it's been a case of "one step forward and two steps back" sometimes. I was satisfied with a simplified text based site but, I also wanted ti challenge myself. AI is not perfect, yet so, this site has been off and on. 

 The past week or so, I've been giving myself a day or two in between updates. I have the type of personality that would allow me to work non-stop for days at a time. However, more often than not, it leads to burn out, and the occasional desire to burn it all down. 

 I like this, though. I think there's long term potential. So, instead of beating myself up over ignoring the project for a day, I'm embracing the rest, and trusting the ebb and flow of creative spark.

jots.title: Are AI's Purposefully Ridiculous?
jots.content:
I've almost given up on every image and video I've tried to create with generative AI. It's got me thinking. Sometimes, it gets so close to what I imagined but, I make one slight change, and the whole thing just becomes silly. 

 Is that on purpose? Do they deliberately screw things up so remarkably to get us to keep creating? They do that with social media, rage baiting. They do that with tech, forcing us to upgrade. Is it out of the realm of possibility that this "AI Boom" is simply more of the same?
